claim: Ion channel models are the building blocks of computational neuron models.
source: Ion channel models are the building blocks of computational neuron models.
evidence: This is a foundational statement in the abstract that establishes the importance of ion channel models in computational neuroscience.

claim: The biological fidelity of ion channel models is crucial for the interpretation of simulations.
source: Their biological fidelity is therefore crucial for the interpretation of simulations.
evidence: This statement follows logically from the role of ion channel models as building blocks and represents established understanding in computational neuroscience.

claim: The number of published ion channel models and lack of standardization make comparison difficult.
source: However, the number of published models, and the lack of standardization, make the comparison of ion channel models with one another and with experimental data difficult.
evidence: This claim is supported by the motivation for the study and is demonstrated through the analysis of ModelDB presented in the results.

claim: 2378 models of voltage- and calcium-gated ion channels coded in NEURON were assigned to 211 clusters.
source: Using annotated metadata and responses to a set of voltage-clamp protocols, we assigned 2378 models of voltage- and calcium-gated ion channels coded in NEURON to 211 clusters.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by the clustering analysis performed on the ModelDB database.

claim: The IonChannelGenealogy web interface provides an interactive resource for categorization of ion channel models.
source: The IonChannelGenealogy (ICGenealogy) web interface provides an interactive resource for the categorization of new and existing models and experimental recordings.
evidence: This describes a deliverable of the study that is referenced throughout the manuscript.

claim: Ion channels play crucial roles in neuronal signal processing.
source: Ion channels play crucial roles in neuronal signal processing (Koch and Segev, 2000; Cai et al., 2004; Goldberg et al., 2008) and plasticity (Sjöström and Nelson, 2002; Shah et al., 2010; Debanne et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Ion channels play crucial roles in neuronal plasticity.
source: Ion channels play crucial roles in neuronal signal processing (Koch and Segev, 2000; Cai et al., 2004; Goldberg et al., 2008) and plasticity (Sjöström and Nelson, 2002; Shah et al., 2010; Debanne et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Interactions among different ion channels in a single cell can lead to extraordinarily complex dynamics.
source: Interactions among the many different ion channels expressed by a single cell can lead to extraordinarily complex dynamics, whose dissection necessitates computational modeling, as first demonstrated by Hodgkin and Huxley (1952a) for action potential generation.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to the foundational Hodgkin and Huxley work and represents established knowledge in the field.

claim: Hodgkin and Huxley first demonstrated that computational modeling is necessary for dissecting complex ion channel dynamics in action potential generation.
source: Interactions among the many different ion channels expressed by a single cell can lead to extraordinarily complex dynamics, whose dissection necessitates computational modeling, as first demonstrated by Hodgkin and Huxley (1952a) for action potential generation.
evidence: This is a historical claim supported by citation to the seminal Hodgkin and Huxley 1952 paper.

claim: NEURON is a simulation environment that can be used to create biophysical neuron models with realistic morphologies, ionic currents, and channel densities.
source: Simulation environments like NEURON (Hines and Carnevale, 2001; Carnevale and Hines, 2006) can be used to create biophysical neuron models with realistic morphologies, ionic currents, and channel densities (Figure 1A), facilitating the integration of experimental data into models (Mainen and Sejnowski, 1995; Stuart and Spruston, 1998; Migliore et al., 1999; Poirazi et al., 2003; Destexhe and Paré, 1999; Traub et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to the NEURON documentation and examples of its use, as well as Figure 1A showing the components of biophysical neuron models.

claim: More than a thousand neuronal models are archived in ModelDB.
source: More than a thousand neuronal models, and several thousand individual ion channel models, are archived in the online database ModelDB (Hines et al., 2004), which enables other researchers to verify original claims, and to reuse and extend existing neuron models in the light of new results.
evidence: This is a factual claim about the ModelDB database, supported by citation.

claim: Several thousand individual ion channel models are archived in ModelDB.
source: More than a thousand neuronal models, and several thousand individual ion channel models, are archived in the online database ModelDB (Hines et al., 2004), which enables other researchers to verify original claims, and to reuse and extend existing neuron models in the light of new results.
evidence: This is a factual claim about the ModelDB database, supported by citation.

claim: Replacing the A-type potassium channel model in a layer 2/3 pyramidal neuron model with different A-type models from ModelDB changes the neuron's dynamics.
source: However, the dynamics can change, sometimes dramatically, when one of the modeled ion channel currents is exchanged for an identically-labeled model from a different publication on ModelDB (Figure 1B, colored traces, Figure 1C).
evidence: This claim is demonstrated by the simulation results shown in Figure 1B and 1C, where different ion channel models produce different neuronal behaviors.

claim: Over 300 new ion channel models were added to ModelDB in 2014 alone.
source: Furthermore, the increasingly large number of models on ModelDB (e.g., over 300 new ion channel models in 2014 alone; Shepherd Lab [2015]), with non-standardized labeling and a high degree of redundancy, makes it difficult to understand how ion channel models relate to each other and to biology.
evidence: This is a factual claim about ModelDB growth, supported by citation to Shepherd Lab 2015.

claim: There are over 250 A-type potassium channel models on ModelDB.
source: For example, a researcher looking to use an existing A-type potassium channel model will find over 250 A-type models, spanning a range of behaviors (Figure 1C, blue).
evidence: This is a factual claim about the number of A-type models in ModelDB, demonstrated in the analysis and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: A-type potassium channel models on ModelDB span a range of behaviors.
source: For example, a researcher looking to use an existing A-type potassium channel model will find over 250 A-type models, spanning a range of behaviors (Figure 1C, blue).
evidence: This claim is demonstrated by the simulation results shown in Figure 1C, where different A-type models produce different outcomes.

claim: It is common for modelers to adapt previously published ion channel models for their own purposes.
source: Instead of a thorough and time-consuming fitting of appropriate ion channel dynamics, it is common for modelers to adapt previously published ion channel models for their own purposes.
evidence: This is an observation about modeling practice, supported by the genealogy analysis showing ancestor-descendant relationships among models.

claim: Adapting previously published ion channel models may introduce experimentally unverified systematic changes or errors into later generations of models.
source: However, this may introduce experimentally unverified systematic changes or even errors into later generations of models and may have dramatic effects on the biological interpretation of the results.
evidence: This is a speculative claim about potential consequences of model reuse, based on logical inference.

claim: The study cataloged all relevant information about each ion channel model from the associated literature, including pedigree relations.
source: We cataloged all relevant information about each ion channel model from the associated literature, including its pedigree relations: whether a given ion channel model is based on previous models, and, if so, which ones.
evidence: This describes a methodological approach taken in the study.

claim: The study compared the kinetics of each ion channel model in standardized voltage-clamp protocols.
source: Additionally, we compared the kinetics of each ion channel model in standardized voltage-clamp protocols.
evidence: This describes a key methodological approach of the study, detailed in the Methods section.

claim: The study grouped 2378 ion channel models into 211 clusters.
source: Our efforts have grouped 2378 ion channel models into 211 clusters, dramatically simplifying the search for an appropriate ion channel model.
evidence: This is a primary result of the study, supported by the clustering analysis.

claim: The underlying database is freely and programmatically accessible via a web API.
source: The underlying database is freely and programmatically accessible via a web application programming interface (API).
evidence: This describes a feature of the resource created by the study.

claim: The resource allows uploading and assessment of experimentally recorded current traces.
source: In an effort to make our resource compatible with experimental data and new ion channel models, we offer the possibility to upload and assess the similarity of experimentally recorded current traces (as well as new models and model traces) in the same topology.
evidence: This describes a capability of the resource, demonstrated in Figure 6.

claim: The study analyzed an unclassified ion channel model as an example of using the comparison framework.
source: We show an example of the use of this comparison through the analysis of an unclassified ion channel model, as well as an experimentally recorded voltage-dependent potassium current from Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: This describes an example application shown in the results, specifically in Figure 6B.

claim: The study analyzed an experimentally recorded voltage-dependent potassium current from Drosophila melanogaster.
source: We show an example of the use of this comparison through the analysis of an unclassified ion channel model, as well as an experimentally recorded voltage-dependent potassium current from Drosophila melanogaster.
evidence: This describes an example application shown in the results, specifically in Figure 6C.

claim: The study categorized 2378 voltage- and calcium-dependent ion channel models in NEURON available on ModelDB.
source: To build a map of ion channel model function, we categorized and analyzed a widely-used subset of 2378 voltage- and calcium-dependent ion channel models ('.mod' files) in the NEURON simulation environment (Hines and Carnevale, 2001; Carnevale and Hines, 2006).
evidence: This describes the scope of the analysis performed in the study.

claim: Metadata was extracted manually from associated journal articles for each ion channel model file.
source: A set of 'metadata' was extracted manually from the associated journal articles for each ion channel model file (Figure 2A, top): reference information (Ref. Info, including author(s) of the model code), ion channel information (I.C. Info: ion selectivity, gating mode, subtype), system information (Sys. Info: brain area, neuron type, neuron region, animal model), as well as additional comments (Other: e.g. temperature constraints, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the methodology for metadata collection, illustrated in Figure 2A.

claim: The majority of all ion channel models (~75%) fell into five classes based on ion selectivity and gating mode.
source: Based on ion selectivity and gating mode, the majority of all ion channel models (~75%) fell into five classes (Figure 2B): voltage-dependent potassium (Kv), voltage-dependent sodium (Nav), voltage- dependent calcium (Cav), calcium-dependent potassium (KCa) and hyperpolarization-activated cation (Ih) channel models.
evidence: This is a result of the classification analysis, shown in Figure 2B.

claim: 74 different subtype labels were recorded across all five ion channel classes.
source: We recorded 74 different subtype labels across all classes (Kv: 32, Nav: 19, Cav: 20, KCa: 11, Ih: 5; Figure 2B, cf. Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the metadata analysis.

claim: Prominent modeled neuron types were pyramidal, interneuron, granule cell, and basket cell.
source: Prominent modeled neuron types were pyramidal, interneuron, granule cell, and basket cell (Figure 2C), and prominent brain areas included hippocampus, and cortex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from the metadata analysis, shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Prominent brain areas modeled included hippocampus and cortex.
source: Prominent modeled neuron types were pyramidal, interneuron, granule cell, and basket cell (Figure 2C), and prominent brain areas included hippocampus, and cortex (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a result from the metadata analysis, shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Many ion channel models form large families with a highly-cited hub model that has many descendants.
source: Visualizing family relationships makes it apparent that many ion channel models form large families, often with a highly-cited hub model that has many descendants (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is an observation from the genealogy analysis, illustrated in Figure 2E.

claim: There are a large number of small families and model singletons that imply de novo ion channel model creation, lack of appropriate citations, or translation from other simulators.
source: On the other hand, there are a large number of small families and model singletons that imply de novo ion channel model creation, lack of appropriate citations, or translation from other simulators (noted in the metadatum comments).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the genealogy analysis results, with possible explanations inferred from the data.

claim: Subtype labeling mapped well onto families, but family identity did not guarantee homogeneity of subtype or vice versa.
source: Subtype labeling mapped well onto families, but family identity did not guarantee homogeneity of subtype or vice versa – all individual subtypes were found across several families (see Figure 2E for Kv, and Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2A,F for other ion type classes).
evidence: This is an observation from comparing subtype labels with family relationships, shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Five voltage-clamp simulation protocols were used to quantify functional relationships between ion channel models.
source: To quantify the functional relationships between ion channel models, we used a set of voltage-clamp simulation protocols, in kind with those developed for the experimental characterization of ion channels and model fitting (Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952b; Willms et al., 1999; Ranjan et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study, with citations to related work.

claim: The voltage-clamp protocols were designed to probe activation, deactivation, inactivation, temporal dynamics during voltage ramping, and repeated action potentials.
source: The protocols were designed to probe the gating characteristics of ion channels, that is, activation, deactivation and inactivation, as well as temporal dynamics during voltage ramping and repeated action potentials.
evidence: This describes the design rationale for the voltage-clamp protocols used in the study.

claim: Principal component analysis was used to obtain a D-dimensional score for each ion channel model, accounting for at least 99% of variance.
source: Using principal component analysis (PCA) across all traces of a particular ion channel type, we obtained a final D-dimensional score for each ion channel model, accounting for at least 99% of the variance across all channel models in each class.
evidence: This describes the dimensionality reduction methodology used in the analysis.

claim: The dimensionality D varied between 16 and 29 dimensions for the five ion channel classes.
source: The dimensionality D varied between 16 and 29 dimensions for the five classes (Kv: 16, Nav: 21, Cav: 29, KCa: 16, Ih: 16).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the PCA analysis.

claim: Ward's clustering method was used to establish an agglomerative hierarchy of ion channel model clusters.
source: Finally, we used Ward's clustering method (Ward, 1963) on the model scores to establish an agglomerative hierarchy of ion channel model clusters (Figure 3C, bottom).
evidence: This describes the clustering methodology, with citation to Ward 1963.

claim: The Kv class was divided into 60 clusters with distinct responses.
source: For the Kv class, this resulted in 60 clusters with distinct responses (Figure 4) and small intra-cluster variability (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a result of the clustering analysis for the Kv class.

claim: The Nav, Cav, KCa, and Ih classes divided into 38, 43, 44, and 26 clusters respectively.
source: The other classes divided similarly into 38, 43, 44, and 26 clusters for Nav, Cav, KCa, and Ih, respectively (see Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2).
evidence: This is a result of the clustering analysis for the other ion channel classes.

claim: Most ancestor-descendant families fell within one cluster, indicating consistency between family relations and ion channel model behavior.
source: We found that most ancestor-descendant families fell within one cluster, indicating consistency between the family relations collected from the papers and ion channel model behavior (Figure 4A–B, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2B,C and G,H).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing genealogy with clustering results, shown in the referenced figures.

claim: A common subtype label did not guarantee a common cluster identity.
source: However, a common subtype label did not guarantee a common cluster identity (Figure 4B, Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2C,H).
evidence: This is a finding from comparing subtype labels with clustering results.

claim: The ~250 A-type-labeled Kv ion channel models fell into 14 clusters.
source: For example, the ~250 A-type-labeled Kv ion channel models fell into 14 clusters (although only five clusters comprised over 90% of them, Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a specific result from the clustering analysis of A-type Kv models.

claim: Five A-type Kv clusters comprised over 90% of A-type models.
source: For example, the ~250 A-type-labeled Kv ion channel models fell into 14 clusters (although only five clusters comprised over 90% of them, Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the clustering analysis.

claim: For four of the five ion type classes (KCa being the exception), most isolated single-model clusters corresponded to genealogical singletons.
source: Interestingly, for four of the five ion type classes (KCa being the exception), most isolated single-model clusters corresponded to genealogical singletons, supporting the idea that these ion channel models are indeed unique, and do not appear isolated simply due to missing ancestor-descendant links.
evidence: This is an observation from comparing clustering results with genealogy data.

claim: Individual neurons of any given type display heterogeneity in ion channel expression and regulation.
source: There is substantial evidence that individual neurons of any given type display heterogeneity in ion channel expression and regulation (Marder and Goaillard, 2006; Schulz et al., 2008).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Characterizing an ionic current using the average response across a population may not be sufficient to capture appropriate behavior at the neuronal level.
source: Furthermore, characterizing an ionic current using the average response across a population may not be sufficient to capture the appropriate behavior at the neuronal level (Golowasch et al., 2002), as there may be several distinct 'solutions' (Prinz et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to published literature.

claim: Diversity and variation in ionic currents within a single cell type may arise from mechanisms such as splice variants, differential subunit combination, and post-translational modification.
source: Diversity and variation in ionic currents even within a single cell type may arise from such mechanisms as splice variants, differential subunit combination, and post-translational modification like phosphorylation (Schulz et al., 2008; Li et al., 2007; Campiglio and Flucher, 2015; Levitan, 1994; Misonou et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: The behavior of groups of ion channel models defined by common subtype, neuron type and brain area is often more diverse than that of models defined by a common cluster.
source: Consistent with this notion, the behavior of groups of ion channel models defined by common subtype, neuron type and brain area (Figure 5A, plotted data points) is often more diverse than that of models defined by a common cluster (Figure 5A, dashed line).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis comparing metadata-based groupings with cluster-based groupings, shown in Figure 5A.

claim: There is no clear correspondence of any given cluster with categories such as brain area and neuron type.
source: More specifically, we find no clear correspondence of any given cluster with categories such as brain area and neuron type (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the analysis, illustrated in Figure 5B.

claim: Nearly every cluster contains ion channel models that have been used in pyramidal cells of both cortex and hippocampus.
source: Nearly every cluster contains ion channel models that have been used in pyramidal cells (Figure 5B, left, blue) of both cortex and hippocampus (Figure 5B, right, blue and green).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: A-type-labeled models used in pyramidal cells of the hippocampus (117 models) are found in nine clusters.
source: In the same vein, e.g., A-type-labeled models that have been used in pyramidal cells of the hippocampus (117 models) are found in nine clusters (cf. ICGenealogy, 2016).
evidence: This is a specific quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: The analysis framework enables automated analysis of new ion channel models.
source: Our analysis framework, accessible through the web interface, enables the automated analysis of new ion channel models as well as experimental data (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes a capability of the resource, illustrated in Figure 6A.

claim: The analysis framework enables automated analysis of experimental data.
source: Our analysis framework, accessible through the web interface, enables the automated analysis of new ion channel models as well as experimental data (Figure 6A).
evidence: This describes a capability of the resource, illustrated in Figure 6A and demonstrated in Figure 6C.

claim: An uncatalogued Kv model from a hippocampus CA1 pyramidal cell model (kad.mod from Hsu et al. 2015) fits well within a cluster of mostly pyramidal A-type-labeled ion channel models used in simulations of rodent hippocampus.
source: We found that the ion channel model fits well within a cluster of mostly pyramidal A-type-labeled ion channel models used in simulations of rodent hippocampus, thereby verifying the assumed characteristics of the model.
evidence: This is a result from the example analysis of a new model, shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Voltage-gated cationic currents across the membranes of Drosophila Kenyon cells are thought to be dominated by A-type K+ channels, in particular Shal/Kv4.
source: Voltage-gated cationic currents across the membranes of these neurons are thought to be dominated by A-type K+ channels, in particular Shal/Kv4 (Gasque et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Gasque et al. 2005.

claim: Experimental recordings from Drosophila Kenyon cells revealed a close match to a mammalian Kv4 ion channel model (Kv4_csi, ModelDB ID no. 145672).
source: The comparison revealed a close match to an existing model from our resource, and thus characterizes the behavior of the ion channel as similar to a mammalian Kv4 ion channel (Figure 6C; Fineberg et al. (2012); Kv4_csi, ModelDB ID no. 145672).
evidence: This is a result from the experimental data comparison, shown in Figure 6C.

claim: The study performed a meta-analysis of voltage- and calcium-dependent ion channel models coded in NEURON available in ModelDB.
source: Here, we have performed a meta-analysis of voltage- and calcium-dependent ion channel models coded in the NEURON programming language available in the database ModelDB (Hines et al., 2004).
evidence: This describes the scope and nature of the study.

claim: The approach of combining metadata with kinetics-based analysis allowed detailed information regarding the identity of each ion channel model.
source: Our approach of combining metadata extracted from publications with a kinetics-based analysis allowed us to provide detailed information regarding the identity of each ion channel model in the resource, filling in missing or ambiguous data, and validating the functional properties of channel models against their sometimes ambiguous nomenclature.
evidence: This describes the contribution of the study's methodology.

claim: The framework provides a unified characterization of ion channel function for large-scale comparison of models with each other and with experiments.
source: Furthermore, we provide a framework for the large-scale comparison of models, both with each other and with experiments using the same standardized protocols, thus paving the way towards a unified characterization of ion channel function.
evidence: This describes the contribution and potential impact of the study.

claim: The voltage-clamp protocols used were designed to efficiently probe the kinetics of all ion channel types considered.
source: The voltage-clamp protocols used in this study were designed to efficiently probe the kinetics of all ion channel types considered here (Hodgkin and Huxley, 1952b; Willms et al., 1999; Ranjan et al., 2011).
evidence: This describes the design rationale for the protocols, with supporting citations.

claim: Measuring kinetic responses allowed comparison of models regardless of their specific implementation.
source: Measuring the kinetic responses of each channel model allowed us to compare models regardless of their specific implementation.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the methodology used.

claim: There is evidence that simple step and ramp current pulses are sufficient to probe the underlying kinetics of neurons.
source: However, there is evidence that simple step and ramp current pulses are sufficient to probe the underlying kinetics of neurons (Druckmann et al., 2011), similar to the voltage-clamp protocols that we use here.
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Druckmann et al. 2011.

claim: The simplicity of the protocols makes experimental comparison easier.
source: Additionally, the simplicity of our protocols makes experimental comparison easier.
evidence: This is a stated advantage of the protocol design.

claim: The study limited analysis to voltage-dependent and calcium-dependent ion channel models coded in NEURON.
source: We limited our analysis to voltage-dependent and calcium-dependent ion channel models coded in the NEURON language, but, given the appropriate protocols, other types of ion-channels can be included.
evidence: This describes the scope and limitations of the study.

claim: The same protocols can be used to integrate models written for other simulators or simulator-independent formats like NeuroML.
source: The same protocols can also be used to integrate models written for other simulators, or even simulator-independent formats, e.g., NeuroML (Cannon et al., 2014).
evidence: This describes potential extensions of the approach, with citation to NeuroML.

claim: Of the 2378 models in the resource, 1132 models were identified as unique.
source: Of the 2378 models in our resource, we could identify 1132 models as unique, and further reduced this to 211 groups with substantially different kinetics.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: The 1132 unique models were further reduced to 211 groups with substantially different kinetics.
source: Of the 2378 models in our resource, we could identify 1132 models as unique, and further reduced this to 211 groups with substantially different kinetics.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis.

claim: The partition of channel models into clusters does not imply that models in the same cluster are necessarily redundant.
source: However, this does not eliminate the task of finding the most appropriate ion channel model current, and we stress that the partition of channel models into clusters of similar response properties does not imply that models in the same cluster are necessarily redundant.
evidence: This is a cautionary statement about interpreting the clustering results.

claim: Intra-cluster differences may still be important depending on the particular simulation at hand.
source: Intra-cluster differences may still be important depending on the particular simulation at hand.
evidence: This is a cautionary statement about the practical use of the clustering results.

claim: The responses of different channels vary slowly and continuously rather than in discrete steps along the dimensions of the manifold of scores.
source: Since the responses of different channels vary slowly and continuously rather than in discrete steps along the dimensions of the manifold of scores (see e.g. Figure 4B), the data may also be amenable to more sophisticated clustering and machine-learning approaches.
evidence: This is an observation about the structure of the data, with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: The raw response data and scores have been made publicly available.
source: To this end, the raw response data and scores have been made publicly available (ICGenealogy, 2016).
evidence: This describes a data availability feature of the resource.

claim: The variability in behavior of ionic currents suggests there is no clear answer to which ion channel model to use for a given neuronal simulation.
source: Furthermore, the variability in behavior of ionic currents seen here and elsewhere (Marder and Goaillard, 2006) suggests that there is no clear answer to the question of which ion channel model (and parameters) to use for a given neuronal simulation at hand.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the findings, with supporting citation.

claim: Neuron model parameters should be viewed as regions rather than as individual representative points in parameter space.
source: On a larger scope, it has been suggested previously that neuron model parameters should be viewed as regions, rather than as individual representative points in parameter space (Goldman et al., 2001).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to Goldman et al. 2001.

claim: The variability at the level of individual ion channel models may cover regions in parameter space and organize into distinct 'solutions' to particular model behaviors.
source: It may be possible that the variability seen at the level of individual ion channel models covers such regions, and organizes into a handful of distinct 'solutions' to particular model behaviors on the neuronal scale (O'Leary et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a speculative claim about the interpretation of variability, with supporting citation.

claim: The database could be used for systematic analyses of co-variability of sets of published ion channel models that elicit desired behaviors in conductance-based neuron models.
source: In this sense, our database would lend itself to systematic analyses of the co-variability of sets of published ion channel models that are able to elicit desired behaviors in conductance-based neuron models (see also Figure 1), in line with previous work (Prinz et al., 2003).
evidence: This describes a potential application of the resource, with supporting citation.

claim: The interactive browser acts as a complement to existing resources such as ModelDB.
source: We provide an interactive browser (ICGenealogy, 2016), which acts as a complement to existing resources such as ModelDB.
evidence: This describes the relationship of the resource to existing databases.

claim: The voltage-clamp protocols are inspired by experimental procedures, allowing direct comparison of ion channel models to experiments.
source: Because our voltage-clamp protocols are inspired by experimental procedures, ion channel models can be compared directly to experiments in an automated fashion.
evidence: This describes an advantage of the protocol design for experimental comparison.

claim: The resource will enable better experimentally-constrained modeling.
source: Beyond its usefulness for cataloguing ion channel model behavior and pedigree, our resource will enable better experimentally-constrained modeling, and presents a first step towards a unified functional map of ion channel dynamics in model and experiment.
evidence: This is a statement about the expected impact of the resource.

claim: The resource presents a first step towards a unified functional map of ion channel dynamics in model and experiment.
source: Beyond its usefulness for cataloguing ion channel model behavior and pedigree, our resource will enable better experimentally-constrained modeling, and presents a first step towards a unified functional map of ion channel dynamics in model and experiment.
evidence: This is a statement about the contribution and future direction of the work.

claim: A layer 2/3 pyramidal cell model was adapted from Traub et al. (2003), ModelDB ID no. 20756.
source: A model of a layer 2/3 pyramidal cell was adapted from a previous study (Traub et al., 2003), ModelDB ID no. 20756.
evidence: This describes the source of the neuron model used in Figure 1.

claim: A total of 3495 .mod files were collected from ModelDB.
source: The total number of files collected from the database was 3495.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the data collection process.

claim: 366 .mod files were tools, full neuron models, or other items that do not function as ion channel models.
source: A total of 3495 .mod files were collected from ModelDB. 366 of these files were tools, full neuron models, or other items that do not function as ion channel models.
evidence: This describes the filtering process applied to the collected files.

claim: The five ion channel groups (Kv, Nav, Cav, KCa, Ih) accounted for 2378 files.
source: These five groups accounted for 2378 files, references for which are available in Supplementary file 2.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the classification process.

claim: A substantial number of .mod files (952 files) had to be slightly modified to work with the procedure.
source: A substantial number of .mod files (952 files) had to be slightly modified to work with the procedure, in one of the following ways: (1) reversal potential was renamed and made a global variable to be accessed from .hoc file, (2) NONSPECIFIC CURRENT was changed to a USEION statement with the correct ion type (3) extra functions and/or data were included through .inc files, data tables or extra .mod files (4) max conductance was made nonzero (arbitrarily set to 1.0) (5) file was split into multiple files for each current present (6) POINTER variables were removed (7) internal temperature initialization was removed, and temperature dependence was set to use the global variable 'celsius'.
evidence: This describes modifications made to enable analysis of the models.

claim: 44 .mod files were omitted from the analysis due to problems with running the simulation protocols.
source: A small number of .mod files were omitted from the analysis due to problems with running the simulation protocols (44 files, Figure 3—source data 1).
evidence: This describes files that could not be analyzed.

claim: Version 7.3 of the NEURON language was used to run the simulation protocols.
source: The most recent version at the time of writing, version 7.3, of the NEURON language (Carnevale and Hines, 2014) was used to run the simulation protocols.
evidence: This describes the software version used in the analysis.

claim: All simulations were run in Ubuntu 12.04.5 on a single core of an Intel Core i7 @ 2.67 GHz with 24 Gigabytes of RAM.
source: All simulations were run in Ubuntu 12.04.5 on a single core of a Intel Core i7 @ 2.67 GHz with 24 Gigabytes of RAM.
evidence: This describes the computational environment used for simulations.

claim: The maximum current amplitude depends on the number of channel models in a particular area and is not related to the kinetic behavior of the channels.
source: We reasoned that the maximum current amplitude depends on the number of channel models in a particular area and was thus not related to the kinetic behavior of the channels.
evidence: This is a rationale for the normalization procedure.

claim: Ward's minimal variance linkage for hierarchical clustering was used as implemented in the MATLAB Statistics Toolbox.
source: For clustering of channel scores, we used Ward's minimal variance linkage (Ward, 1963) for hierarchical clustering, as implemented in the MATLAB Statistics Toolbox (R2015A, The MathWorks Inc., Natick, MA).
evidence: This describes the clustering method and software used.

claim: Several cluster indexes were employed to determine an appropriate number of clusters: Silhouette criterion, Dunn index, Davies-Bouldin index, and Calinski-Harabasz measure.
source: To this end we employed a range of internal clustering evaluation measures, which indicate the emergence of an appropriate number of clusters. Although the evaluation of these measures requires some heuristics, they have been well established and can guide the decision as to which number of clusters to choose. Concretely, these are: the Silhouette criterion (Rousseeuw, 1987), the Dunn index (Dunn, 1973), the Davies-Bouldin index (Davies and Bouldin, 1979), and the Calinski-Harabasz measure (Calinski and Harabasz, 1974), also implemented in the MATLAB Statistics Toolbox (R2015A, The MathWorks Inc., Natick, MA).
evidence: This describes the methodology for determining cluster numbers, with citations to the methods.
